_meta.source: MOE admissions pages and school ECG practice
_meta.notes: Asks are free because asking costs courage, not hours: a hand of five, two playable a year, and playing one draws another. Commitments spend points because three months is three months. Every flag set here is read by a callback card, which is the whole promise of a move: do it now, and the story remembers.

rule: Two kinds. Superpowers are asks: free, held in a hand of five, two a year, and using one teaches me another. Commitments take real time, so they sit among my choices and spend my points.

moves.label: Get help with the subject I dread
moves.body: Go to the teacher after class. Say which part I do not get. That is the whole move.
moves.outcome: The teacher shows me where it actually went wrong, which is never where I thought.
moves.missed: The subject I dread stayed the subject I dread.

moves.label: Book a chat with my ECG counsellor
moves.body: Every secondary school and JC has one, and it is free. Bring one question. Where could I go is a good one.
moves.outcome: They show me two roads I did not know existed. Nobody makes me take either.

moves.label: Ask my Year Head what moving up takes
moves.body: Not a promise. A question: what would my marks need to look like to take this at G3?
moves.outcome: Now I know the number. It is smaller than the rumour said.

moves.label: Tell my parents what I actually want
moves.body: They have a plan for me. They cannot compare it with mine if mine stays secret.
moves.outcome: One awkward dinner. After it, one fewer thing to carry alone.

moves.label: Ask for a job shadowing day
moves.body: My school or a family friend can set one up. One day watching someone actually do the job.
moves.outcome: The job is not what I imagined. Better or worse, now I know which.
moves.missed: The shadowing day ran with somebody else asking the questions.

moves.label: Prepare for my Early Admissions interview
moves.body: EAE shortlists me, then interviews me, and some courses set an aptitude test. Most people arrive having prepared nothing.
moves.outcome: I practise saying out loud why this course, with the folder open beside me. The panel asks exactly that, and I have an answer.
moves.check: Ask the course whether it interviews, tests, or both.
moves.missed: The interview came around with no rehearsal behind it.

moves.label: Ask what my talent counts for in DSA
moves.body: DSA takes Sec 4s into JC on talent: sport, CCA, a subject I am unusually good at. Fair warning, an accepted offer is binding. I am choosing, not keeping options.
moves.outcome: Early Admissions weighs it for a polytechnic course, and an arts school reads it on a portfolio. Naming it changes how I treat it.
moves.check: DSA for junior colleges, at moe.gov.sg. Accepted offers commit me to that JC.
moves.missed: The talent stayed a hobby nobody at an admissions desk heard about.

moves.label: Treat my attachment like a real job
moves.body: Poly internships and ITE attachments are where employers first see me. Show up like it is the job, because it is.
moves.outcome: My supervisor writes three sentences about me at the end. People read those.
moves.missed: The attachment stayed a timetable entry.

moves.label: Put my name down for a semester abroad
moves.body: Poly, ITE and uni all run overseas stints. The form is shorter than the queue for it is.
moves.outcome: Three months somewhere nothing works the way I assume. I come back harder to rattle.
moves.missed: The exchange cohort flew without me.

moves.label: Ask a working adult for one hour
moves.body: Find one person doing the thing I want. Ask for an hour and bring questions. Most people say yes and nobody asks them.
moves.outcome: One hour of how it really works, which no website has.

moves.label: Ask the teacher who knows me best which subject fits
moves.body: They see me every week and they have an opinion. Nobody ever asks for it.
moves.outcome: They name something I am good at that I had not counted as a skill.

moves.label: Ask a senior who took the road I want
moves.body: One year above me, same school, already there. Ask what they wish they had known.
moves.outcome: Straight answers, no brochure voice. Some of it puts me off, which is also useful.

moves.label: Go to an open house and ask one real question
moves.body: Everyone walks around collecting flyers. Ask a lecturer what students find hardest in year one.
moves.outcome: The answer is specific and nothing like the flyer. I remember it for years.

moves.label: Ask my CCA teacher for something harder
moves.body: Not a bigger title. A real job nobody wants: run the thing, teach the juniors, fix what is broken.
moves.outcome: I am trusted with something before I feel ready, which is how it always goes.

moves.label: Ask someone in my family who took another road
moves.body: An uncle, a cousin, anyone who did not do what everyone expected. Ask how it worked out.
moves.outcome: Someone in my own family is proof the standard road is not the only one.

moves.label: Ask my lecturer how they got into this
moves.body: Poly and ITE lecturers worked in the trade before they taught it. Most are glad to be asked.
moves.outcome: They tell me the route they actually took, which was not the neat one on the website.

moves.label: Book a session with my campus career centre
moves.body: Poly, ITE and every university run one. They know which employers hire from my course, and it is free while I am enrolled.
moves.outcome: They read my resume properly and tell me the two things wrong with it.

moves.label: Ask my supervisor what would get me promoted
moves.body: Not a complaint. A question: what would I need to be doing for this to be the obvious next step?
moves.outcome: They name two things. One I expected. The other I had never thought about.

moves.label: Ask how somebody got the life I want
moves.body: Not their job. Their week. How they got the hours to look like that.
moves.outcome: It was arranged on purpose, in steps, and they will tell me the steps if I ask.

moves.label: Ask somebody younger to teach me something
moves.body: They know the tools I have been avoiding. Asking costs me nothing but the admission.
moves.outcome: Half an hour, and the thing I was dreading turns out to be learnable.

moves.label: Tell the people at home what might change
moves.body: A change at forty lands on everyone I live with. Say it out loud before it is decided.
moves.outcome: They had noticed. Saying it makes it a plan the household is in on, not a surprise.

moves.label: Put my name up for class comm or EXCO
moves.body: Class committee, CCA committee, house, prefect, peer support.
moves.outcome: I get the role and the clipboard, and the term teaches me what carrying something actually costs.
moves.missed: Somebody else took the clipboard this year.
moves.check: Ask my form teacher when nominations open.

moves.label: Lead my VIA project instead of attending it
moves.body: Values in Action, planned by I rather than handed to me.
moves.outcome: I pick who it serves, arrange it, and write what changed. It reads completely differently in an application.
moves.missed: The VIA hours got collected. Nothing else did.
moves.check: Ask who signs off a student proposed VIA project.

moves.label: Tutor a younger student every week
moves.body: One hour a week, same student, all term.
moves.outcome: Explaining it badly twice is how I find out I only half knew it. By June I know it cold.
moves.missed: Nobody was tutored, and the topic stayed half known.
moves.check: Ask whether my school runs a peer tutoring scheme.
